arxiv-2002-11945.title: Is my Neural Network Neuromorphic? Taxonomy, Recent Trends and Future Directions in Neuromorphic Engineering
arxiv-2002-11945.creator: Sumon Kumar Bose, Jyotibdha Acharya, Arindam Basu
arxiv-2002-11945.description: A 2020 arXiv research paper by Sumon Kumar Bose, Jyotibdha Acharya, Arindam Basu. In this paper, we review recent work published over the last 3 years under the umbrella of Neuromorphic engineering to analyze what are the common features among such systems. We see that there is no clear consensus but each system has one or more of the following features:(1) Analog computing (2) Non von-Neumann Architecture and low-precision digital processing (3) Spiking Neural Networks (SNN) with components closely related to biology.

arxiv-2311-11555.title: NePF: Neural Photon Field for Single-Stage Inverse Rendering
arxiv-2311-11555.creator: Tuen-Yue Tsui Qin Zou
arxiv-2311-11555.description: A 2023 arXiv research paper by Tuen-Yue Tsui Qin Zou. We present a novel single-stage framework, Neural Photon Field (NePF), to address the ill-posed inverse rendering from multi-view images. Contrary to previous methods that recover the geometry, material, and illumination in multiple stages and extract the properties from various multi-layer perceptrons across different neural fields, we question such complexities and introduce our method - a single-stage framework that uniformly recovers all properties.

arxiv-2402-09863.title: Double-well instantons in finite volume
arxiv-2402-09863.creator: Wen-Yuan Ai, Jean Alexandre, Matthias Carosi, Björn Garbrecht, and Silvia Pla
arxiv-2402-09863.description: A 2024 arXiv research paper by Wen-Yuan Ai, Jean Alexandre, Matthias Carosi, Björn Garbrecht, and Silvia Pla. Assuming a toroidal space with finite volume, we derive analytically the full one-loop vacuum energy for a scalar field tunnelling between two degenerate vacua, taking into account discrete momentum. The Casimir energy is computed for an arbitrary number of dimensions using the Abel-Plana formula, while the one-loop instanton functional determinant is evaluated using the Green’s functions for the fluctuation operators.

arxiv-2407-02870.title: Membership Inference Attacks Against Time-Series Models
arxiv-2407-02870.creator: Noam Koren, Abigail Goldsteen, Guy Amit, Ariel Farkash
arxiv-2407-02870.description: A 2024 arXiv research paper by Noam Koren, Abigail Goldsteen, Guy Amit, Ariel Farkash. Analyzing time-series data that contains personal information, particularly in the medical field, presents serious privacy concerns. Sensitive health data from patients is often used to train machine learning models for diagnostics and ongoing care. Assessing the privacy risk of such models is crucial to making knowledgeable decisions on whether to use a model in production or share it with third parties.

arxiv-2409-11942.creator: Fen Long 1 , Shangyun Wang 2 , Songbai Chen 3,4 , Jiliang Jing 3,4
arxiv-2409-11942.description: Abstract Abstract Recently, magnetic reconnection has attracted considerable attention as a novel energy extraction mechanism, relying on the rapid reconnection of magnetic field lines within the ergosphere. We have investigated the properties of the energy extraction via magnetic reconnection in a Konoplya-Zhidenko rotating non-Kerr black hole spacetime with an extra deformation parameter.

arxiv-2411-16984.description: Abstract . We prove eigenvalue bounds for Schrödinger operator − Δ g + V -\Delta_{g}+V on compact manifolds with complex potentials V V . The bounds depend only on an L q L^{q} -norm of the potential, and they are shown to be optimal, in a certain sense, on the round sphere and more general Zoll manifolds.

arxiv-2503-11480.description: Abstract At finite lattice spacing, Lagrangian and Hamiltonian predictions differ due to discretization effects. In the Hamiltonian limit, i.e. at vanishing temporal lattice spacing a t a_{t} , the path integral approach in the Lagrangian formalism reproduces the results of the Hamiltonian theory.

arxiv-2505-05779.title: A note on quantum Hamiltonian reduction and anomalies
arxiv-2505-05779.creator: Boris M. Elfimov, Alexey A. Sharapov
arxiv-2505-05779.description: Abstract . Quantization of field-theoretic models with gauge symmetries is often obstructed by quantum anomalies. It is commonly believed that the origin of these anomalies lies in the infinite number of degrees of freedom, which requires completing the model within an appropriate regularization scheme.

arxiv-2505-15639.title: Time reversal of reflected Brownian motion with Poissonian resetting
arxiv-2505-15639.creator: Fausto Colantoni, Mirko D’Ovidio, Gianni Pagnini
arxiv-2505-15639.description: Abstract In this paper, we study reflecting Brownian motion with Poissonian resetting. After providing a probabilistic description of the phenomenon using jump diffusions and semigroups, we analyze the time-reversed process starting from the stationary measure. We prove that the time-reversed process is a Brownian motion with a negative drift and non-local boundary conditions at zero.

arxiv-2506-02232.title: Investigating the Reasonable Effectiveness of Speaker Pre-Trained Models and their Synergistic Power for SingMOS Prediction
arxiv-2506-02232.creator: Orchid Chetia, Girish*, Mohd Mujtaba, Swarup Ranjan, Pailla Balakrishna, Arun Balaji, Rajesh
arxiv-2506-02232.description: Abstract In this study, we focus on Singing Voice Mean Opinion Score (SingMOS) prediction. Previous research have shown the performance benefit with the use of state-of-the-art (SOTA) pre-trained models (PTMs). However, they haven’t explored speaker recognition speech PTMs (SPTMs) such as x-vector, ECAPA and we hypothesize that it will be the most effective for SingMOS prediction.

arxiv-2509-13475.description: Abstract Background: Understanding the experimental B ⁡ ( E ​ 2 ) B(E2) values for Sn isotopes around 110 Sn has been a significant challenge in nuclear structure studies for over a decade. Both experimental data and many, though not all, calculations suggest a picture of the light Sn isotopes as being quadrupole-soft, that is, spherical, yet easy to deform.

To investigate the propagation effects and small-scale fading differences between MMW and conventional CMW ( CMW ) bands, multi-band channel measurements have to be conducted. One key parameter to characterize small-scale fading is the Rician K -factor.

arxiv-2601-18248.creator: Mohammad Aghaie, and Ryosuke Sato
arxiv-2601-18248.description: Abstract Recently, Ai, Cruz, Garbrecht, and Tamarit (ACGT) 2 ; 4 ; 3 ; 5 claimed that there is no strong CP problem by adopting a new order of limits in the volume and topological sector. We critically examine this proposal by focusing on simple one-dimensional quantum mechanics on a ring.

arxiv-2602-15275.title: To boost or not to boost, that’s the question
arxiv-2602-15275.creator: Yu Nakayama
arxiv-2602-15275.description: A 2026 arXiv research paper by Yu Nakayama. Or should we talk about dS/CFT correspondence or dS/SFT correspondence in cosmological correlators? In non-unitary field theories—which are conjectured to be dual to cosmological correlators—scale invariance does not necessarily imply full conformal invariance. While general relativity predicts the emergence of conformal invariance (or boost symmetry in the bulk), various modified theories of gravity suggest only scale invariance, characterized by the absence of bulk boost symmetry. We demonstrate this distinction using Einstein-Aether theory as a canonical example.

pmc-12655510.description: Background: Current disease-modifying therapies (DMTs) for multiple sclerosis (MS) attenuate pathogenic immune responses but are limited by safety and tolerability concerns. LPX-TI641, an orally bioavailable, clinical-stage small-molecule agonist of Tim-3/4, represents an antigen-independent strategy to restore immune tolerance by expanding regulatory T cells (Tregs).
